articles.title: Xbox’s Forza Studios Have Been Tag-Teaming For Years. Now They’re Becoming One
articles.summary: Big changes are afoot at Microsoft, as the company announced a massive reorganization of its Xbox gaming division. While Activision and Bethesda will expand their remit, adding several studios to their portfolio, Forza series developers Playground and Turn 10 won't be included in the consolidation.
body: "These two studios have been creative and franchise partners for over a decade, and today’s changes will formally move their work into one team," Xbox chief creative officer Matt Booty wrote in a letter to employees. What the letter doesn't precisely mention is if there'll be layoffs at these studios, but we do know that 268 positions at Xbox are being made redundant as part of a previously announced second wave of job cuts. Mergers typically see several roles overlap, so it won't be too surprising to see people let go from both studios as they start the process of becoming a single team.

Playground Games has a storied career, having developed the first Forza Horizon game, released in 2012. Since then, the studio has developed each entry in the franchise, which slowly overtook the main Forza Motorsport series to become one of Xbox's tentpole franchises. Forza Horizon 6 was released earlier this year to positive reviews, and next year will bring a new chapter in the Fable series. Turn 10 Studios is an even older developer, having been established in 2001 to develop racing games for Microsoft Game Studios.
points: Big changes are afoot at Microsoft, as the company announced a massive reorganization of its Xbox gaming division.

articles.title: Bloodborne’s JackSepticEye Says He’s A “Vibe-Checker” For The Movie
articles.summary: When the R-rated Bloodborne movie was officially announced with YouTuber Seán McLoughlin AKA JackSepticEye signed on as a producer, many wondered what, exactly, his involvement might be. Now, we have a better idea.
body: Appearing on 100 Questions with Tom Simons ( via GamesRadar ), McLoughlin said you can think of his role as a producer as a "vibe-checker" for the movie. In essence, McLoughlin said that when he's on calls with stakeholders discussing key elements of the "vetting process" and hiring, he speaks up and helps make decisions.

He went on to say that he's not trying to shepherd the Bloodborne movie to become "the game," or a movie that tries to "one up the game" or compete with it. Instead, McLoughlin said his ambition is to "honor the universe that's there and tell as good a story as I can within it."

Before this, McLoughlin said he's not trying to make a quick buck with the Bloodborne movie, though if the movie is a success, it stands to reason that he would participate in that given his status as a producer. He has spoken about his extreme passion for the franchise, saying he believes working on the Bloodborne movie is what he was put on this Earth to do.
Bloodborne is not the only From Software game getting a film adaptation, as a live-action Elden Ring is on the way from director Alex Garland and A24.

articles.title: LEGO Teases Dragon Ball Sets
articles.summary: Rumors have been percolating around the internet for a while, but LEGO just confirmed it: Dragon Ball LEGO sets are coming soon. A short video teaser posted to LEGO’s website and social pages shows six Dragon Balls gathered, followed by a seventh rolling in.
body: Assuming this teaser plays out like other recent LEGO announcements, we can expect to see details of LEGO’s upcoming Dragon Ball set(s) in the coming weeks.

For now, there’s no word on any specific Dragon Ball sets or release dates. The furthest-out release date for any announced LEGO sets is January 1, which is when the LEGO Super Mario minifigure sets will hit store shelves (some of those sets are available for preorder now).
Dragon Ball was created by Akira Toriyama as an anime TV series that ran from 1986 - 1989 in Japan. It has since turned into a whole franchise of additional TV series, movies, video games, and more.

LEGO’s teaser shows six Dragon Balls, yellow-orange spheres with varying numbers of red stars on them. While six Dragon Balls together have no special power, introducing the seventh makes them able to summon their Eternal Dragon, who can grant wishes. That’s what’s implied when the seventh ball rolls in during the teaser video, right before it ends.

articles.title: State Of Decay 3 Lives On, And Is Still Coming To Game Pass
articles.summary: In the wake of the latest round of reshuffles and retrenchments, Microsoft has confirmed that State of Decay 3 developer, Undead Labs, has reached an agreement with a new publisher that will keep the game alive.
body: Undead Labs will now continue working on State of Decay 3, with Microsoft confirming that the game will still launch on Xbox Game Pass day-one when its ready. The studio confirmed the news in an announcement of its own, confirming that it is now a completely "independent, employee-owned game development studio."

"We're enormously grateful for our years as part of XBOX and for everything that relationship has made possible," says Philip Holt, Studio Head of Undead Labs. "Microsoft has been part of the State of Decay story from the very beginning, and we’re proud of everything we’ve accomplished together."

Undead Labs was just one of several studios that Microsoft has offloaded in recent months, with Double Fine and Compulsion Games similarly finding futures away from the Xbox publishing arm. Ninja Theory has been less successful; however, the studio now on the brink of closure.

articles.title: Nodusfall Hands-On Preview: It’s Hoyoverse’s New One About Squadding Up and Killing Really, Really Big Monsters
articles.summary: I didn’t know anything about Nodusfall coming into it, but I came out very, very impressed by it. It’s no secret that the action game is in something of a bad way at the moment. Most things are kind of sauceless, a well-done steak.
body: They told us that the Maldrake, the last of the three bosses my team squadded up against in Nodusfall, would be the one that would really try us. But it was the Qiongqi that really tested our group, wiping out our entire party the first time we attempted him. “Okay,” I said to our team. “Let’s do that again, but good this time.” Someone else pointed out that we hadn’t really been using our potions (I for the record, had, but I was just being judicious). We took a second to regroup and crack a couple more jokes, and then we ran back into the fight.

In my experience with Nodusfall, that means squadding up with some folks and killing really, really big monsters. But first, I had to select a character. After fooling around with my options for a bit, I settled on a woman with a fire sword who believed the best defense was a good offense. As I landed hits, I would build up a bar I could cash in for stronger, fiery-er (that’s a thing, right?) heavy attacks. The rest of my squad saddled up with an archer, a magic user/healer, and a large man in armor with a massive greatsword who served as our tank.

articles.title: Blizzard Reveals the World of Warcraft Forever Feature 'We Simply Must Hold the Line On'
articles.summary: Ever since Blizzard revealed World of Warcraft: Forever at Blizzcon 2026, the company has been laser-focused on maintaining its Classic+ identity, even if that means not implementing some quality-of-life features the game's retail version has had for years.
body: In a reply to GingiTV and Nobbel87, two of the biggest WoW personalities on X/Twitter (albeit from complete opposite ends of the community), Blizzard developer Josh Greenfield confirmed that not implementing shared drops and tagging was "one of those things that we simply must hold the line on." He continued, saying "It’s hard to see the value in something like this when you are frustrated in the moment but it is extremely important to our social pillar to maintain some of this friction."

In the retail version of World of Warcraft, players who are questing or trying to farm rare spawns can all tag the same enemy (to a limit), so that everyone can get the rewards for killing it. This makes it a lot easier to play the game outside of a group, but it all but eliminates the need to group up with other players outside of high-end group content like dungeons and raids.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Taking Over Miami, One Airlifted Letter At A Time
articles.summary: Ahead of its release in November, the marketing for Grand Theft Auto 6 has begun to take over Miami's Kaseya Center. As part of the campaign, developer Rockstar Games and publisher Take-Two Interactive are decking out the stadium in giant GTA 6 letters that will spell out "Welcome to Vice City"…
body: The advertising campaign is reportedly valued at almost $1 million for Miami-Dade County (via WLRN ), and the funds will go toward developing a plot of land behind the stadium for community use. The deal has been criticized by the county Sheriff’s Office, with Commissioner Bermudez proposing that the funds instead go toward funding gaps in the law division's budget.

Alongside Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz, Bermudez also criticized GTA 6 for glorifying crime and the killing of police officers. While you can commit those acts in GTA 6, it looks like getting away with literal murder will be more challenging, as the game's new Wanted and Honor systems will make cops a lot smarter and more persistent when compared to previous games in the series.

Rockstar Games has also officially announced Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album. This is a 34-song collection of original music from performers like Keith Richards, Yung Lean, and Morgan Wallen, and it also includes several licensed tracks. Unlike the game, a physical edition is available to preorder, and it'll be released on November 19, the same day as GTA 6.

articles.title: Sega Planned to Kill Sonic the Hedgehog Before Movie Success
articles.summary: Sega bosses were ready to ditch Sonic the Hedgehog before the franchise's hugely-successful live-action movie helped change their minds. That's according to Sonic Team leader and development veteran Takashi Iizuka, who has worked as a designer, director and producer on more than 30 games featuring…
body: While the idea of Sega ditching Sonic seems shocking — akin to Pokémon abandoning Pikachu, or Mario shaving off his moustache — the Sonic series has certainly faced some tough years. Indeed, as Iizuka has now admitted, his tenure in charge of the blue blur included "good times" and also "the worst times."

"It has been 35 years, which means it has been longer than actually my children, so I look upon this franchise like sort of like my own son," Iizuka told One More Game. "There had been good times, and there had been bad times... during the worst times, I was told by the higher-ups that we should cancel the entire franchise.

"I had to fight within the organization to keep the franchise as long as possible," Iizuka continued. "The biggest milestone for me was the first movie, that had been a great hit and definitely changed the course of this franchise."

articles.title: Sega Once Floated Cancelling Sonic the Hedgehog, but the Movies Changed Everything
articles.summary: 2026 marks the 35th anniversary of the Sonic franchise, an impressive milestone for one of gaming's most iconic mascots. Though the series has had its ups and downs, and at one point that almost meant cancellation.
body: Reflecting on the series in a conversation with the press (as reported by One More Game ), Iizuka revealed that "during the worst times, I was told by the higher-ups that we should cancel the entire franchise." In response, Iizuka had to "fight within the organization to keep the franchise as long as possible." While he doesn't give details on when Sega was floating cancellation or how long that period lasted, It is only in recent years that the series has regained momentum.

Iizuka noted that the biggest success for the franchise was the release of the first movie in 2020. Despite early backlash to Sonic's original design, the film was eventually released to massive box-office success. This showed Sega that there was still interest in the series while also helping to introduce a new generation of fans to the character. It "changed the course of this franchise," said Iizuka.

articles.title: Netflix Officially Announces Next 'KPop Demon Hunters' Project
articles.summary: KPop Demon Hunters diehards have something new to look forward to. Netflix just announced KPop Demon Hunters: The Immersive Experience, an in-person interactive event offered at select Netflix House locations. The press release describes it as “an all-new interactive, music-filled adventure.”
body: As for the specifics, Netflix says the experience begins backstage with Huntr/x before the opening night of their world tour. Then the film’s main antagonist, Gwi-Ma, attacks the venue, and guests will join Huntr/x in battling demons via interactive sets and screens, as well as 3D technology. The storyline will be presented through music and play-based challenges featuring live actors and custom animation. The event plays out to the film’s soundtrack, featuring songs like “Golden” and “How It’s Done.”

Fans don’t just want to watch KPop Demon Hunters, they want to live in the world of HUNTR/X. Netflix House is where fandoms like this get to live year-round, so it’s the perfect home for everything KPop Demon Hunters fans have been asking for. Singing the songs they already know by heart, facing off with demons, hanging out with Derpy Tiger — every detail is built so fans of all ages can feel, hear, and see this world exactly the way they imagined it.

articles.title: Xbox confirms 268 more layoffs, further studio closures, and Obsidian's shift to Bethesda as major restructuring continues
articles.summary: Following reports that further job cuts were imminent at Xbox, Microsoft has confirmed more sweeping changes as its major restructuring continues. As a result, some Xbox studios will combine, others are set for closure, and 268 more layoffs have been announced.
body: In July, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced job cuts affecting 3,200 employees as part of what she called the "most significant" restructuring the company had ever undertaken. 1,600 of those layoffs were effective immediately, while some first-pary studios, including Double Fine and Compulsion Games, were permitted to go independent again.

And with the threat of 1,600 more cuts hanging over the heads of remaining employees, Sharma has swung the axe again. This time, layoffs will affect 268 employees across Halo Studios, other unspecified first-party studios, and members of Xbox Game Studios ' "management and central functions layer".
points: Following reports that further job cuts were imminent at Xbox, Microsoft has confirmed more sweeping changes as its major restructuring continues.
As a result, some Xbox studios will combine, others are set for closure, and 268 more layoffs have been announced.

articles.title: Garfield’s New Video Game Is GOTY…for 4th Graders
articles.summary: But I know that there was a time when I wouldn’t have cared about that. As a kid, my entire personality was Garfield. I was a card-carrying member of the official Garfield Fan Club, owned more merchandise than you can imagine, and would love any video game that simply put Garfield’s face on screen.
body: I have never struggled to review a video game as much as I have with Garfield: Escape From Monday. There’s a very easy version of this review in front of me: one where I sit here dunking on Microids’ low-budget 3D platformer, and throw in a few lasagna jokes for cheap pop. It would be warranted, even, considering that there is virtually nothing noteworthy about Escape From Monday ’s slapdash design. It’s a platformer pulled from a filing cabinet and dressed up with Garfield characters.
And so, I enlisted the help of my 4th grade self to get some fresh perspective.
Giovanni Colantonio: Before we get started, let’s get to know more about you. Well, I mean, I kind of know everything about you already, but for the sake of our readers, who are you?
Young Giovanni: hi im giovanni. i am in the fourth grade and i go to dale street school. my favorite color is red, and i like video games and cartoons. my favorite cartoon is garfield!

articles.title: It's The End of An Era For 'Halo' and 'Fallout' As Xbox Reshapes Studios
articles.summary: Five months after laying off 1,600 employees, Xbox has announced that it will continue consolidating its workforce. Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty announced Tuesday that 268 additional employees across various Xbox departments are being laid off, and a number of first-party studios will be…
body: Four major brands on Xbox will be impacted by these changes: Halo, Fallout, Forza, and Fable.

In a new blog post, Booty announced that the next Halo title will be developed by Activision. The game will be produced by a new team, but a smaller group of employees at Halo Studios will continue to offer support to the franchise as well. Activision will continue overseeing the Call of Duty franchise, Booty said.

Obsidian, the studio best known for Fallout: New Vegas, will now operate under Bethesda. Microsoft says that Obsidian's current projects — like the next Fallout game — will continue as planned. Per earlier reports, the new Fallout game is expected to be headed by New Vegas lead director Josh Sawyer. Bethesda at large continues to focus on The Elder Scrolls 6, but the studio began pre-production on Fallout 5 earlier in 2026.

Playground and Turn 10 will fully merge together as one studio that focuses on Forza and Fable. "King will expand its remit to include Microsoft Casual Games, uniting our two global leaders in casual game design and live operations," the post continues.

articles.title: Hellblade developer Ninja Theory heading towards closure in new wave of Xbox cuts, as two separate agreements collapse
articles.summary: Ninja Theory - developer of the Hellblade series of games, Enslaved: Odyssey to the West, DmC: Devil May Cry, and Heavenly Sword - is entering consultation in preperation for the studio's closure as part of today's sweeping Xbox cuts and layoffs.
body: Announced by a new Xbox Wire blog post penned by Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty, Ninja Theory employees and Xbox will begin a consultation process as the studio looks to head towards a closure.

The blog post reads: "Unfortunately, two separate agreements for Ninja Theory fell through. We will now begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward."

Ninja Theory had seemed safe during Xbox's initial wave of job and studio cuts in July, having apparently entered a partnership to an unnamed company. But that seems to have changed, leaving Ninja Theory without an owner and unable to continue operation.

The studio was developing Senua, a new entry in the studios' Hellblade action adventure series - a game only announced in June as part of an Xbox Games Showcase. Senua was said to be a larger, " more expansive " game compared to previous entries in the series. Within a month of its reveal Ninja Theory was put up for sale by Microsoft.

articles.title: Next major Halo game being developed by Activision, as Halo Studios all but closes as part of Microsoft's Xbox restructuring
articles.summary: Halo Studios (formerly 343 Industries) won't develop the next mainline Halo game because it's being what sounds like drastically reduced in size. Microsoft has instead given development duty to Activision, which is making "a new purpose-built team" separate to Call of Duty to make it.
body: "We are eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer," Xbox Studios boss Matt Booty wrote in a statement. "Activision will also be developing the next Halo title, led by a new, purpose-built team that is separate from ongoing development and plans for Call of Duty. A small team at Halo Studios will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market," Booty wrote.

In a statement provided to Kotaku, Activision president Rob Kostich said: "We're thrilled to welcome Halo, Rare, and World's Edge to Activision." (Rare is also going to Activision.) "It's an honor and a responsibility that we do not take lightly. These teams and their games have inspired fans around the world for decades.

"For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place. It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community."

videos.title: I strongly recommend: Control Resonant (Review)
videos.summary: Thanks to Nvidia for sponsoring the video. To learn more about how Nvidia tech delivers the best possible fidelity and performance in games like Control Resonant, click the link:
body: Control Resonant adopts the structure and aesthetic of a Ubisoft style open world game full of map markers and regional bosses, but whereas in a Ubisoft game the structure is the experience, here the structure is the beginning of a process that is specifically designed to subvert expectations. Rather than dictate the game's ultimate form, the structure is simply a scaffold that exists to let Remedy build other, more interesting things.

videos.title: DF Direct Weekly #282: 007 First Light Path Tracing, Kingmakers Gameplay, New GPUs Delayed To 2028?
videos.summary: Thanks to Alienware for sponsoring DF Direct. To learn more about the Alienware AREA-51 Gaming Desktop, check out:
body: In a bit of a slow week for news, the team goes hands-on with a bunch of cool games to present their findings - principal amongst them being 007 First Light's visually stunning, but incredibly taxing path tracing upgrade. Redemption Road's 12-minute Kingmakers gameplay deep dive impresses the panel before Tom delivers his thoughts on Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave on Switch 2, with Oliver testing Diablo 4 also on the Nintendo hybrid. Meanwhile, reliable leaker Kepler_L2 says that we're only looking at one new GPU launch in 2027 - and it looks like the desktop version of the same GPU slated to appear in Microsoft's Project Helix...
